purpose: Primary-source evidence for a static GRE Mathematics Subject Test practice simulator.

verifiedCurrentRules.scoreScaleCaveat: Each test edition normally occupies only part of the overall score scale. Scaled scores depend on edition-specific equating, not a universal percentage formula.
verifiedCurrentRules.endingDecision: The Subject Test has a report/view-or-cancel-scores decision at the end. Official scores are released later; immediate item-by-item review is a practice feature.

visualEvidence.localReferenceDescription: The provided image shows a GRE General Test quantitative comparison question, Section 3 of 5 / Question 1 of 12, with a calculator button. It is not a Mathematics Subject Test screenshot.
visualEvidence.officialReviewEvidence: ETS's current Subject Test strategies page uses an old General Test review screenshot as its example. The review table has Number, Status, and Marked columns and Return / Go to Question controls. The selected question is highlighted and columns can be sorted.
visualEvidence.incompleteStatusCaveat: The General Test example also uses Incomplete for multiple-selection questions. Mathematics Subject Test items each have one correct answer among five options, so that state is unnecessary.
visualEvidence.unseenQuestionCaveat: The General Test screenshot text disallows direct jumps to Not Encountered questions. No separate modern Subject Test screen was verified; this particular restriction is visual-reference evidence, not an independently verified current Subject-specific rule.

historicalScoring.rounding: Round the raw total to the nearest integer before looking up the form-specific conversion table.
historicalScoring.comparability: ETS rescaled Mathematics effective October 2001. Pre-October-2001 scaled scores should not be compared with later Mathematics scores.
historicalScoring.penaltyChangeDate: Not established by the primary sources consulted; do not imply the penalty disappeared only with September 2023 computer delivery.
historicalScoring.implementationImplication: Show current correct-only practice performance separately from any explicitly labeled historical booklet-scaled estimate. Do not apply a historical penalty conversion table to the current correct-only score as though it were current ETS equating.

latestOfficialPracticeBook.scoring: Number correct, without a wrong-answer deduction.

implementationLimits: No complete public, authenticated modern Mathematics Subject Test interface walkthrough was located. Present the design as an ETS-style practice reconstruction rather than an exact official clone.
The local reference's calculator and multi-section structure belong to the General Test and should not be copied into Subject Test mechanics.
Saving, pausing, extra keyboard shortcuts, post-test correct answers, and immediate scores are practice conveniences rather than verified live-test features.
Timer visibility and five-minute behavior are documented for other ETS computer tests, but the exact Subject Test warning behavior was not independently verified.
